newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack, Virgin agree tilt-train upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack, Virgin agree tilt-train upgrade.

text.p: Railtrack Plc and Virgin Rail Group, owned by millionaire Richard Branson's private Virgin Group, said on Thursday they had agreed the terms of an infrastructure upgrade package to allow Virgin to operate high-speed tilting trains on its main intercity routes.

Railtrack, responsible for the maintenance and development of most of Britain's fixed rail infrastructure, had offered to strike an upgrade deal with the eventual winner of the West Coast Main Line (WCML) train operator linking London to centres including Glasgow, Manchester, Liverpool and Birmingham.
It plans to invest 1.5 billion pounds in the WCML network.

These investments provide in the region of 200 million stg of extra passenger-related spending, in addition to about 1.3 billion stg already budgeted for such improvements as purchasing and installing a high-tech signalling system, and making track and power improvements.

Industry sources say the collaboration plan will be one of the first big tests of Britain's newly-privatised railway business as it will require the commercial interests of a major player in train operating and those of Railtrack to be brought together.

Virgin Rail director Will Whitehorn said the intention was to achieve a 200 kilometre per hour (kph) railway by 2002, though he said that operating trains at significantly higher speeds would take a few more years.
Currently the line's maximum speed is 175 kph.
"We view this agreement as a commercial partnership and both parties intend to build on it with the ambition of creating a 225 kph service by 2005," he said.
In the short term, he added, travellers would expect a reliable railway under its new ownership "and Virgin and Railtrack will make that the priority for the next year".
In winning the WCML franchise, Virgin put forward a detailed plan to transform the service from conventional to tilting
